item.title: Evolving role of proton therapy in contemporary oncology.
item.dc:creator: Lebow ES, Shih HA
item.description:
Authors: Lebow ES, Shih HA
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70622
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42870507



Abstract:
Proton therapy offers a distinct physical advantage over photon radiotherapy through the Bragg peak dose concentration in target with both lower integral dose and finite path length, and sharper penumbra as compared to photons, collectively reducing radiation exposure to surrounding normal tissues and potentially improving the therapeutic ratio. However, this advantage is tempered by uncertainties, including range uncertainty and variable relative biological effectiveness. In this review, the authors summarize contemporary evidence supporting proton therapy across pediatric, central nervous system (CNS), head and neck, thoracic, breast, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, and hematologic malignancies, as well as reirradiation. The strength of evidence varies substantially by disease site. Proton therapy is well established in pediatric cancers and selected CNS tumors, where minimizing integral dose and late toxicity is especially important. Randomized trials have demonstrated clinically meaningful benefits in selected settings, including improved disease control and survival with proton craniospinal irradiation for leptomeningeal metastases and reduced toxicity with preserved disease control and survival benefit in oropharyngeal cancer. Conversely, randomized data in localized prostate cancer have not shown improved patient reported outcomes compared with intensity modulated photon therapy. Ongoing phase 3 trials across multiple disease sites are expected to further define the role of protons by clarifying comparative effectiveness, toxicity reduction, and cost-effectiveness relative to advanced photon techniques. Future progress will depend on improved patient selection, robust treatment planning, and emerging technologies including adaptive proton therapy, proton arc therapy, and FLASH radiotherapy.

item.title: Perioperative immunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Hörner M, Hartmann S, Adkins DR, Uppaluri R
item.description:
Authors: Hörner M, Hartmann S, Adkins DR, Uppaluri R
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70642
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42844879



Abstract:
Outcomes for patients with resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remain suboptimal despite multimodal therapy, with high rates of recurrence and patients suffering from toxicity of treatments. Immune checkpoint inhibitors, which have transformed the management of recurrent and metastatic disease, have been advanced into the perioperative and adjuvant settings. Recent phase III trials mark a turning point: the addition of adjuvant nivolumab improved disease-free survival in pathologic high-risk resected HNSCCs, while perioperative pembrolizumab significantly prolonged event-free survival in resectable locally advanced HNSCCs, supporting a shift toward integrated perioperative immunotherapy strategies. Although the former approach fits into a conventional adjuvant framework, biological insights suggest that neoadjuvant delivery enables effective immune priming extending therapeutic approaches. Together, these advances redefine therapeutic strategies in resectable HNSCC and highlight the potential of perioperative immunotherapy to improve long-term outcomes.

item.title: Orbital Abscess Complicating Allergic Fungal Rhinosinusitis Due to Streptococcus halichoeri: A Rare Zoonotic Sinonasal Infection.
item.dc:creator: Bashiri S, Lutfeali S, Grein J, Tang DM, Wu AW
item.description:
Authors: Bashiri S, Lutfeali S, Grein J, Tang DM, Wu AW
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261497528
Published: 2026-Oct-14
PMID: 42870632



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary bacterial infections complicating allergic fungal rhinosinusitis (AFRS) are uncommon but can be serious given the expansile nature of the disease which can thin and erode the bone separating the sinuses from the brain and orbits. Zoonotic pathogens are rarely implicated as pathogens. CASE REPORT: A 21-year-old African American male with several years of progressive nasal obstruction, facial pressure, and hyposmia, presented emergently with acute left eye pain and swelling, diplopia, afferent pupillary defect and inferior visual field deficit. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute on chronic sinusitis with a left orbital abscess. The patient underwent emergent endoscopic sinus surgery with left orbitotomy and drainage of the orbital abscess. Intraoperative findings, pathology, cultures, and allergy testing were reviewed demonstrating AFRS and a novel zoonotic bacterium, Streptococcus halichoeri. CONCLUSIONS: This case represents the first otolaryngologic case of S. halichoeri infection, a severe and complicated sinus and orbital infection. It is unclear if the severity of this infection was a consequence of the unusual pathogen, of the long-term thinning of the bone around the orbit, or both. Although AFRS is not considered an infection, secondary bacterial infection may occur and cause severe complications. Early surgical intervention and culture-directed therapy are essential in managing complicated sinonasal diseases.

item.title: Wildfire Air Pollution Exposure and Head and Neck Cancer Incidence.
item.dc:creator: Jung YS, Yu SE, Nadeau KC, Cramer J, Xu MJ, Mitchell MB, Chiang S, Ruan M, Lee SE
item.description:
Authors: Jung YS, Yu SE, Nadeau KC, Cramer J, Xu MJ, Mitchell MB, Chiang S, Ruan M, Lee SE
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70874
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42870377



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the association between wildfire-specific particulate matter 2.5 (wPM2.5) exposure and the overall and site-specific incidences of head and neck and aerodigestive cancer (HNC). STUDY DESIGN: Epidemiological retrospective cohort analysis. METHODS: HNC incidence data were derived from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program (2016-2022). The relationship between county-level wPM2.5 exposure metrics and HNC incidence rates were examined using a distributed lag non-linear model, adjusting for health behaviors (tobacco/alcohol use, diet, exercise, and sexual activity), demographics (age, sex, race/ethnicity), population size, and year, with county as a random effect. Lag effects were analyzed over 10 years. HNC subsites included nasal/sinus/ear, nasopharynx, oral cavity, oropharynx (stratified by p16 status), hypopharynx, and larynx. RESULTS: Higher wildfire-specific PM2.5 exposure was associated with increased cumulative HNC incidence over 0-10-year lags, with a cumulative relative risk (cRR) of 1.06 (95% CI: 1.04-1.09) per additional smoke exceedance day, 1.41 (1.24-1.60) for any annual exposure, and 1.23 (1.13-1.33) per percentage-point increase in days above 5 μg/m3. Among subsites, oral cavity cancer showed consistent increases (cRR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.00-1.06), oropharyngeal cancer risk increased to 1.09 (1.06-1.13), and laryngeal cancer exhibited the largest effect, with a cRR of 1.13 (1.07-1.19) per additional exceedance day over a 10-year lag period. When stratified by p16 status, significant associations were noted for p16-positive, p16-negative, and p16-unknown tumors. CONCLUSIONS: Higher frequency, intensity, or persistence of wildfire-smoke exposure is associated with increased HNC risk, with the strongest associations driven by long-term exposures.

item.title: HPV-Positive Keratinizing Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Is Associated With Better Survival: A NCDB Study.
item.dc:creator: Chen H, Bowman T, O'Neil Danis D, Chui KKH, Jawad B, O'Leary M, Tracy J, Soneru C
item.description:
Authors: Chen H, Bowman T, O'Neil Danis D, Chui KKH, Jawad B, O'Leary M, Tracy J, Soneru C
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70999
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42869851



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic relevance of human papillomavirus (HPV) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: The National Cancer Data Base (NCDB) was used to query patients with NPC and available HPV testing data between 2010 and 2017. Logistic regression was performed to predict factors associated with HPV testing and HPV positivity. Overall survival (OS) was evaluated using Kaplan Meier analysis between HPV-positive versus HPV-negative cohorts. Univariate and multivariate analyses using Cox proportional hazards modeling were performed to assess for factors associated with OS. RESULTS: Among our cohort of 5081 patients, 3177 (62.5%) underwent HPV testing. Kaplan Meier analysis revealed improved OS among HPV-positive patients with keratinizing subtype of NPC (log rank p < 0.001). No differences in OS were observed in patients with other histologic subtypes of NPC. On multivariate analysis of the keratinizing SCC cohort, HPV positivity was associated better OS after controlling for sex, age, race, insurance status, facility volume, facility type, zip code level education, Charlson comorbidity score, staging, and treatment (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70-0.94, p = 0.006). CONCLUSION: HPV status was independently associated with improved OS among patients with keratinizing subtype of NPC. Incorporation of HPV testing may be warranted in the workup of NPC.

item.title: Uncertainty quantification for detecting out-of-distribution cases in deep learning segmentation of head and neck organs of interest.
item.dc:creator: van Aalst JE, Simões R, Maruccio FC, MacRae DC, van der Hoek L, Langendijk JA, van Ooijen PMA, Janssen TM, Brouwer CL
item.description:
Authors: van Aalst JE, Simões R, Maruccio FC, MacRae DC, van der Hoek L, Langendijk JA, van Ooijen PMA, Janssen TM, Brouwer CL
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111826
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42869247



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Quality assurance (QA) of auto-segmentations is necessary for safe clinical deployment. Deep learning models are optimised for data similar to their training set, but reliability drops with out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs. This study evaluates whether uncertainty quantification (UQ) can detect OOD inputs arising from distribution shift in head and neck organ of interest (OOI) auto-segmentation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty scores and geometric accuracy of nnU-Net models were evaluated in two experiments. First, as a proof-of-concept, we assessed whether uncertainty scores detect metal artefact (N = 10) from non-artefact cases (N = 10) on a baseline model (mixed training data, N = 620) and a no-metal model (artefact-free training data, N = 620). Second, in a clinically realistic experiment, we split a fine-tuning dataset by uncertainty score to obtain a narrow model (low-uncertainty cases, N = 21) and a broad model (high-uncertainty cases, N = 21). A held-out test set (N = 76) evaluated whether segmentation accuracy differed between uncertainty categories. RESULTS: Both experiments showed that uncertainty scores reflect the learned training distribution. In the supervised experiment, the no-metal model demonstrated greater uncertainty score separation between artefact and non-artefact cases (1.1 × 105 vs 0.6 × 105) than the baseline model (1.1 × 105 vs 0.8 × 105). In the unsupervised experiment, the narrow model performed significantly better on certain than uncertain cases (p = 0.04), while no difference was seen for the broad model (p = 0.34), which did include these cases in training. CONCLUSIONS: Uncertainty quantification can detect distribution shifts in radiotherapy auto-segmentation. This could support automated QA workflows by identifying in-distribution cases and enabling the application of specialised models.

item.title: A randomized, placebo-controlled, phase II study of docetaxel and platinum with or without erlotinib in recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous-cell carcinomas.
item.dc:creator: William WN, Feng L, Kies MS, Ahmed S, Blumenschein GR, Glisson BS, Massarelli E, Johnson FM, Lu C, Le X, et al.
item.description:
Authors: William WN, Feng L, Kies MS, Ahmed S, Blumenschein GR, Glisson BS, Massarelli E, Johnson FM, Lu C, Le X, et al.
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108584
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42868984



Abstract:
PURPOSE: We conducted a randomized phase II trial to evaluate whether adding erlotinib to platinum/docetaxel improves clinical outcomes in the first-line treatment of recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous-cell carcinomas, building on our previous single-arm phase II trial. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This was a placebo-controlled, double-blind, single-center phase II study. Patients (N = 120) were randomly assigned (1 : 1) to receive platinum (carboplatin area under the curve 6 or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 every 21 days for six cycles) plus docetaxel (75 mg/m2 every 21 days for six cycles) with either erlotinib (150 mg/day orally until progression) or placebo. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival, response rates, duration of response, and correlations of erlotinib-induced rash/biomarkers with outcomes. RESULTS: Median PFS was 6.1 months with erlotinib versus 4.4 months with placebo [hazard ratio (HR) 0.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.42-0.95, P = 0.026]. Median overall survival was 17.0 months in the erlotinib arm compared with 13.7 months in the control arm (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.43-1.04, P = 0.0718), meeting the prespecified type I error threshold. Subgroup analyses demonstrated numerically favorable PFS HRs across most clinical subgroups, with a more pronounced benefit observed in patients with oropharyngeal and human papillomavirus-related tumors. Development of grade ≥2 rash during the first cycle of erlotinib was associated with significantly improved overall survival (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.19-0.87, P = 0.021). The addition of erlotinib increased the incidence of grade 2-4 adverse events, particularly gastrointestinal toxicity, rash, fatigue, and dehydration but no unexpected safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: The study met its primary endpoint, supporting the continued relevance of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) inhibition in this disease. Although contemporary immunotherapy-based standards limit direct adoption of this regimen, these results provide clinically meaningful insight into EGFR biology and support further development of modernized, tyrosine kinase inhibitor-based EGFR strategies, including rational combinations and biomarker-driven approaches, to improve outcomes.

item.title: Validation of Immunoscore for Prognostic Stratification in HPV-associated Oropharyngeal Cancer: An International Multicenter Study.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen DH, Majdi A, Marliot F, Houtart V, Kirilovsky A, Hijazi A, Fredriksen T, De Sousa Carvalho N, Bach AS, Gaultier AL, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Nguyen DH, Majdi A, Marliot F, Houtart V, Kirilovsky A, Hijazi A, Fredriksen T, De Sousa Carvalho N, Bach AS, Gaultier AL, et al.
Journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research | DOI: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-1776
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42868274



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Optimizing treatment in HPV-associated OPSCC remains challenging, as current TNM- and smoking-based risk stratification inadequately captures tumor biological heterogeneity, highlighting the need for more prognostic biomarkers. We report the first validation of the Immunoscore (IS) in HPV-associated OPSCC. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We analyzed 191 HPV-associated (p16⁺ and HPV DNA/RNA⁺) OPSCC patients from an international multicenter cohort (2015-2024), including a French monocentric retrospective training cohort (n = 48) and three validation cohorts: French monocentric retrospective (n = 48), French multicenter prospective (n = 50), and US multicenter retrospective (n = 45). IS quantified CD3⁺ and CD8⁺ densities in tumor cores and invasive margins, with cut-offs defined in the training cohort and validated across cohorts. Associations with disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and time to recurrence (TTR) were assessed, alongside 3'RNA-seq and sequential immunofluorescence profiling. RESULTS: Median age 65; 80% male; 74% smokers; 66% T1-2; 82% N0-1. IS-High patients had superior 3-year DFS across cohorts (all log-rank P < .05). Multivariable analysis identified IS-Low as the independent prognostic factor with the largest adjusted effect size for DFS (HR 9.03; 95% CI: 4.02-20.31; P < .001). The combined IS-clinical model showed better DFS prediction than the clinical-only model (C-index 0.82 vs 0.70; P < .0001). Similar results were observed for TTR and OS. IS-High tumors showed enriched lymphoid and myeloid populations, contrasting with immune-poor IS-Low tumors. CONCLUSIONS: IS outperformed clinical variables in prognostic performance. By identifying biologically distinct risk groups, IS may enable biomarker-guided, risk-adapted treatment strategies, including treatment de-escalation and intensification.

item.title: Differential impact of tumor-derived ESR1 mutations on elacestrant benefit in metastatic breast cancer.
item.dc:creator: Sledge GW, Xiu J, Fuqua S, Ribeiro JR, McArthur H, Oberley MJ, Radovich M, Spetzler D, Kaklamani V
item.description:
Authors: Sledge GW, Xiu J, Fuqua S, Ribeiro JR, McArthur H, Oberley MJ, Radovich M, Spetzler D, Kaklamani V
Journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research | DOI: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-2215
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42868272



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: ESR1 mutations are a well-established mechanism of endocrine therapy resistance in estrogen receptor (ER)-positive metastatic breast cancer and are a biomarker for treatment benefit from oral selective estrogen receptor degraders (SERDs) such as elacestrant. However, variant-specific and context-dependent effects on therapy response remain poorly understood. METHODS: Breast tumors carrying ESR1 mutations that underwent DNA sequencing at Caris Life Sciences were studied (n=3,344), with whole-transcriptome sequencing available for a subset (n=1,663). Time-on-treatment (TOT) was obtained from insurance claims and defined as the interval from initiation to discontinuation of elacestrant. Cox proportional hazards models were used to calculate hazard ratios (HRs), and log-rank tests assessed statistical significance. RESULTS: ESR1 mutation frequency increased with longer duration of prior endocrine therapy including combined treatment regimens, particularly those including CDK4/6 inhibitors. Heterogeneity in treatment benefit was observed across ESR1 variants. Tumors harboring ESR1-L536 mutations demonstrated reduced elacestrant benefit, with significantly shorter TOT compared to more common mutations such as Y537 and D538G (HR=2.089, p=0.001). L536-mutated tumors had lower expression of GREB1, a key estrogen-responsive gene, and reduced enrichment of estrogen response pathways, suggesting reduced ER pathway activation compared to other variants. Additionally, patients with multiple ESR1 mutations had significantly shorter TOT compared to those with single mutations (adjusted HR=1.62, p=0.038). CONCLUSIONS: ESR1 mutations are likely not functionally equivalent in their impact on elacestrant benefit. These findings highlight the importance of variant-specific stratification in optimizing endocrine therapy and suggest that biomarkers of ER signaling activity may further refine patient selection for SERD treatment.

item.title: Investigation of salivary microRNAs as non-invasive biomarkers for weaning stress in piglets: A preliminary study.
item.dc:creator: Jeong GH, Park SJ, Lim KS
item.description:
Authors: Jeong GH, Park SJ, Lim KS
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360727
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42868144



Abstract:
Weaning exposes piglets to abrupt nutritional and environmental changes that induce physiological stress. Saliva, unlike serum or tissue samples, enables repeated and stress-free sampling, making it a practical biological matrix for monitoring early-life adaptation. To evaluate whether salivary microRNAs (miRNAs) can serve as non-invasive indicators of these responses, we profiled miRNA expression in saliva collected from suckling and weaning piglets. Small RNA sequencing was conducted to detect salivary miRNAs and a total of 41 differentially expressed miRNAs (DEMs) were detected between the two groups, with 20 showing highly expression and 21 showing lowly expression in weaning piglets. Several of these DEMs have been previously associated with immune activity, inflammatory regulation, oxidative stress responses, and disease processes, highlighting their biological relevance during the weaning transition. Functional annotation of predicted target genes revealed enrichment in pathways such as TGF-beta, HIF-1, and AMPK signaling, as well as autophagy-related processes. These pathways are known to play key roles in stress adaptation, cellular metabolism, and immune modulation. These findings suggest that salivary miRNA profiles may reflect molecular changes associated with the weaning transition and may serve as candidate non-invasive indicators of physiological stress and health status in piglets. This approach may provide a basis for future development of saliva-based monitoring strategies after validation in larger cohorts and cost-effective targeted assays.

item.title: Personalized assessment of high-definition slow-oscillatory transcranial direct current stimulation (so-tDCS) in older adults with sleep and subjective cognitive complaints: A study protocol for a randomized clinical trial.
item.dc:creator: Lu H, Ni X, Yang NS, Yuen YS, Gong Y, Ma SL
item.description:
Authors: Lu H, Ni X, Yang NS, Yuen YS, Gong Y, Ma SL
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360573
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42868122



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is increasingly recognized as an early and potentially modifiable stage in the trajectory of neurodegenerative diseases. In older adults with SCD, untreated sleep disturbances may accelerate the neurodegenerative process, potentially via mechanisms involving amyloid-beta accumulation, and contribute to more rapid cognitive deterioration. Currently, non-pharmacological treatment options that concurrently manage SCD and sleep disturbances remain scarce. High-definition slow-oscillatory transcranial direct current stimulation (so-tDCS) is an emerging, frequency-specific neuromodulation technique designed to enhance brain health and cognition. METHODS AND DESIGN: This is a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial. Right-handed Chinese older adults with SCD and sleep disturbances will be randomly assigned to receive either high-definition 0.75 Hz so-tDCS or sham stimulation over a 4-week intervention period, with 40 participants per group. Outcome measures, including galvanic skin response, subjective cognitive complaints, sleep quality, salivary amyloid-beta levels, and domain-specific cognitive performance, will be evaluated at four time points: baseline, week 4 (immediately post‑intervention), and follow‑up at weeks 8 and 12. CONCLUSIONS: Personalized neurophysiological signals, namely electrode-skin impedance, will be monitored using state-of-the-art measurement during so-tDCS. The successful implement of this signal will provide researchers with access to an "add-on" setting that enables them to easily, quickly and quantitatively evaluate real-time neurophysiological signals, thereby facilitating the incorporation of transcranial brain stimulation into clinical practice. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07433738.

item.title: Maternal opioid prescriptions and subsequent risk of hospital admission in offspring in South Korea: A nationwide birth cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Kim HJ, Yim Y, Nehs CJ, Park J, Kim ES, Cho SJ, Fond G, Boyer L, Kang J, Yon DK
item.description:
Authors: Kim HJ, Yim Y, Nehs CJ, Park J, Kim ES, Cho SJ, Fond G, Boyer L, Kang J, Yon DK
Journal: PLoS medicine | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pmed.1004829
Published: 2026-Oct-01
PMID: 42868097



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal opioid exposure may disrupt infant development and immune system function, potentially increasing long-term susceptibility to hospital admissions. Thus, we aimed to investigate the association between prenatal opioid exposure and the risk of hospital admission in children. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We established a population-based birth cohort in South Korea by linking mothers and children using National Health Insurance Service data and followed from January 1, 2009, to December 31, 2023. We constructed propensity score (PS)-matched and sibling comparison cohorts and performed a multi-pronged approach, including dose-dependent and time-attenuation analyses. All 5,249,429 individuals with eligible children born between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2017, were included (2,236,167 mothers and 3,013,262 children). Infants were followed up for up to 14 years, depending on birth year. Prenatal exposure to opioids was defined as maternal receipt of two or more prescriptions within any given trimester. Adjusted incidence rate ratio (aIRR) of hospital admission among children with prenatal opioid exposure was estimated for causes including infections, non-infectious respiratory conditions, non-infectious gastrointestinal conditions, oral cavity diseases, injuries/external causes, and non-infectious genitourinary conditions. Analyses were adjusted for maternal age at delivery, infant sex, region of residence, household income level, birth season, parity, severe maternal morbidity score, number of outpatient visits and hospital admissions in the year before pregnancy, preterm birth, low birth weight, delivery type, year of delivery, maternal history of substance use and neuropsychiatric disorders, and plurality. Of the 2,928,186 children, we identified 2,809,515 (51.4% male) and 118,671 (51.3% male) infants without and with prenatal opioid exposure, respectively. The rate of hospital admissions in children with prenatal opioid exposure was 28% higher in the PS-matched cohort (aIRR 1.28 [95% CI 1.28, 1.29]; p < 0.001). The association was attenuated in the sibling comparison cohort, indicating the potential influence of shared familial factors, but remained statistically significant (aIRR 1.08 [95% CI 1.07, 1.10]; p < 0.001). Hospital admission rates in children increased in a dose-dependent manner with maternal opioid dose and duration of opioid prescriptions (low-dose exposure: aIRR 1.19 [95% CI 1.19, 1.20]; p < 0.001; high-dose exposure: aIRR 1.40 [95% CI 1.39, 1.41]; p < 0.001). Prenatal opioid exposure was significantly associated with increased rates of hospital admission across several causes of morbidities, including infections, respiratory non-infections, oral cavity, gastrointestinal non-infections, genitourinary non-infections, and injury/external conditions. These associations between prenatal opioid exposure and hospital admission rates in children diminished with age but remained evident up to five years of age. The main limitations of this study's methodology include the use of prescription records, which may not fully capture actual medication intake, and residual confounding that cannot be entirely excluded. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide birth cohort study, maternal opioid prescription during pregnancy was associated with a substantial increase in the risk of hospital admissions in the offspring across various causes of morbidities. Although the attenuated estimates in the sibling comparison analysis suggest that familial factors may partly explain this association, these findings may inform postnatal monitoring and management strategies for children born to mothers who received opioid prescriptions during pregnancy.

item.title: Benefits of optimizing cooperation in head and neck cancer care in a regional referral network.
item.dc:creator: Schutte HW, Labbé N, van den Broek GB, Honings J, Marres HAM, Weijs WLJ, Steens SCA, Arens AIJ, van Engen-van Grunsven ACH, Driessen CML, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Schutte HW, Labbé N, van den Broek GB, Honings J, Marres HAM, Weijs WLJ, Steens SCA, Arens AIJ, van Engen-van Grunsven ACH, Driessen CML, et al.
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10622-0
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867666



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Reducing the time to treatment improves outcomes, including survival, in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC). After implementing multiple local interventions to optimise organisation of HNC care in a large, recognized head and neck oncological centre (HNOC), this observational study evaluates changes in the diagnostic pathway before the first visit to our HNOC following the implementation of a regional referral agreement within a broader programme of care pathway optimisation. METHODS: All patients with newly diagnosed HNC in 2008 were compared with those diagnosed in 2016 before and after the agreement with referring hospitals to immediately refer patients based on clinical suspicion of cancer and refrain from any additional diagnostic procedures. RESULTS: Of the 559 patients with suspected HNC who were eligible for inclusion, 266 were included in 2008 and 293 in 2016. The time from the initial consultation with the referring medical specialist to referral to our HNOC decreased significantly from 16 to 11 days (median, p = 0.002). Overall, the interval from the initial consultation with the referring medical specialist to the start of treatment at an HNOC decreased from 56 days to 38 days (median, p < 0.001). Interestingly, this also resulted in a 47.6% decrease in rigid laryngopharyngoscopies and a 38.9% reduction in CT and MR imaging (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Following the care pathway optimisation, patients started treatment earlier, and the number of diagnostic procedures performed under general anesthesia decreased, reducing associated risks and costs. This study demonstrates that coordinated pathway optimisation at both network and tertiary-centre level may contribute to more efficient oncological care.

item.title: Pathological characteristics rather than thyroid size predict incidental parathyroidectomy during thyroid surgery.
item.dc:creator: Aydın HT, Gökdere OG, Aydın A
item.description:
Authors: Aydın HT, Gökdere OG, Aydın A
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10645-7
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867665



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incidental parathyroidectomy (IP) is a recognized event during thyroid surgery and may contribute to postoperative hypocalcemia and impaired parathyroid function. Although several clinical and operative factors associated with IP have been described, the contribution of thyroid size-related characteristics remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the association between thyroid size-related parameters, clinicopathological characteristics, and the occurrence of IP. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients who underwent thyroidectomy between January 2021 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Patients with primary parathyroid disease were excluded. Demographic, operative, pathological, and thyroid size-related variables, including dominant nodule diameter, thyroid specimen weight, and thyroid lobe dimensions, were analyzed. Associations with incidental parathyroidectomy were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. The multivariable model included age, sex, malignant thyroid pathology, Hashimoto thyroiditis, multinodular goiter/nodular hyperplasia, extent of thyroidectomy, and central neck dissection. RESULTS: The study included 1,049 patients, of whom 125 (11.9%) had incidental parathyroidectomy. Dominant nodule diameter and thyroid specimen weight were not significantly associated with IP in available-case analyses. Increasing largest thyroid lobe diameter was associated with lower odds of IP in univariable analysis, although this association was not robust after adjustment. In the multivariable analysis, malignant thyroid pathology (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.49-4.09; p < 0.001), multinodular goiter/nodular hyperplasia (aOR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.11-4.80; p = 0.025), and female sex (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.01-3.50; p = 0.045) were independently associated with higher odds of IP. Female sex was also associated with higher odds of IP, whereas Hashimoto thyroiditis did not retain statistical significance after multivariable adjustment. Thyroid size-related parameters showed no consistent independent association with IP. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective design, incomplete data for some thyroid size-related parameters, and the possibility of residual confounding.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To define the most distal entry point (MDEP) of the pectoral branch in adult Chinese males, integrate it into a standardised Landmark-Axis-Plane (LAP) skeletonisation workflow for the pectoralis major island flap, and describe its clinical performance under IDEAL Stage 2a. METHODS: The anatomical phase measured the MDEP in 20 formalin-fixed adult Chinese male cadavers (40 hemithoraces). The clinical phase analysed 194 males (skeletonised, n = 74; conventional, n = 120) treated contemporaneously by two surgical teams at a single centre using a target trial emulation framework with propensity-score overlap weighting and logistic regression with robust sandwich variance estimation. The primary endpoint was 30-day Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ III complications. The technique and team were strictly collinear; all estimates are noncausal. RESULTS: The MDEP lay 6.2-6.5 cm below the midclavicular point, predominantly at the third rib or third intercostal space. The LAP workflow was associated with fewer severe complications, but strict technique-team collinearity and sensitivity to unmeasured confounding preclude a causal interpretation. item.title: The clinical outcomes and overall survival in patients with mucoepidermoid and adenoid cystic carcinoma of the salivary glands: A comparative analysis of long-term outcomes.

item.description:

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (MEC) and adenoid cystic carcinoma (AdCC) are the two most common salivary gland malignancies, but differ substantially in biological behavior, recurrence patterns and long-term prognosis. Comparative data from patients treated within the same institution using similar management strategies remain limited. This study compared long-term survival, recurrence patterns and prognostic factors between MEC and AdCC to identify histology-specific characteristics that may inform follow-up and treatment strategies. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients treated for MEC or AdCC at a tertiary academic center between 1996 and 2022. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS) and recurrence patterns, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression. RESULTS: Sixty-two patients (31 AdCC, 31 MEC) were included. Although 5-year OS was identical (81%), AdCC had significantly poorer DFS (53% vs. 80%, p = 0.015) and higher recurrence rates (18/31 vs. 8/31, p = 0.020), and more distant metastases (18/31 vs. 1/31 patients, p = 0.0016). High tumor grade, defined according to tumor-specific pathological criteria, was the strongest independent predictor of poor outcomes (OS: HR = 19.72, p < 0.001; DFS: HR = 3.99, p = 0.01). Advanced T stage, nodal involvement, and metastatic disease independently predicted worse OS. Seven of 11 patients with locoregional recurrence developed a second recurrence, predominantly in AdCC. Curative-intent salvage therapy did not improve OS. CONCLUSIONS: Tumor grade is the strongest prognostic determinant, surpassing histologic subtype. AdCC demonstrates more aggressive biology with higher recurrence rates and poorer DFS despite similar OS. The limited survival benefit of salvage therapy highlights the need for grade-adapted management and more effective therapies for high-grade disease.

item.title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of cerebrospinal fluid leak in skull base surgery: a scoping review.
item.dc:creator: Aydogmus E, Atalay Erdogan B
item.description:

Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10667-1
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867660



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak remains one of the most significant complications of skull base surgery, particularly in endoscopic endonasal and transsphenoidal approaches. Accurate risk stratification may improve surgical planning and reconstruction strategies. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have been increasingly investigated for CSF leak prediction; however, the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to map the current literature and summarize data sources, modeling approaches, validation strategies, and reported performance. METHODS: This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligibility was structured using the Population-Concept-Context framework. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language studies published from 2019 to 2025. Two authors independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts and independently charted data using a standardized table; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Eligible original human studies applied AI/ML to predict perioperative surgical CSF leak or to derive an imaging biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak/encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. No formal protocol was prepared or registered. RESULTS: Fifty-five records were identified, and nine primary studies met the eligibility criteria after duplicate removal and full-text assessment. Six studies predicted intraoperative CSF leak, two predicted postoperative leak, and one evaluated a deep-learning-derived CT biomarker for identifying spontaneous lateral skull-base CSF leak or encephalocele relevant to surgical assessment. Three studies used classical machine-learning methods, four used predominantly deep neural-network or convolutional-neural-network approaches, one compared classical models with a feedforward neural network, and one used a BERT-based natural-language-processing model. One study reported prospective temporal validation; none reported independent external validation at another institution. Among studies reporting AUC, values ranged from 0.69 to 1.00; accuracy, where reported, ranged from 70% to 98.33%. CONCLUSIONS: AI-based prediction of CSF leak is a promising but evolving field. Methodological heterogeneity and the absence of independent external validation constrain clinical translation. Future studies should prioritize standardized outcomes, multicenter datasets, and prospective validation to support integration into clinical decision-making.

item.title: Impact of early combined oral and intratympanic corticosteroid therapy on hearing outcomes in sudden sensorineural hearing loss: A prospective cohort study.

Published: 2026-Oct-13

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate hearing outcomes following early simultaneous oral and intratympanic corticosteroid therapy in patients with sudden sensorineural hearing loss (SSHL). METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted including 65 adult patients with SSHL treated with oral prednisone (1 mg/kg/day; maximum 60 mg/day) for 14 days combined with intratympanic methylprednisolone (40 mg/mL) administered weekly for three weeks. The primary outcomes were changes in pure-tone average (PTA; 500-3000 Hz) and speech discrimination score (SDS) at baseline and one month after treatment. RESULTS: Median baseline PTA improved from 85 dB to 56 dB one month after treatment, corresponding to a median improvement of 28 dB (p < 0.0001). Median SDS increased from 0% to 80% (p < 0.0001). item.title: Predicting malignancy in thyroid AUS: ultrasonographic and clinical risk factors beyond ACR TI-RADS.
item.dc:creator: Kuyumcu OF, Demircioglu O, Tok RN, Toper MH, Girgin S, Asya O

Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867655



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Thyroid cancers often present as nodules, with fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) and ultrasonography as the primary diagnostic tools. Given the variability in clinical approaches and the lack of consensus guidelines, ultrasonography has become increasingly important, particularly for indeterminate cytology. We aim to assess the clinical utility and diagnostic performance of the ACR TI-RADS (American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System), together with cytopathological subtypes, in predicting malignancy in atypia of undetermined significance (AUS) cases. METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre study conducted over 30 months, all AUS cases underwent preoperative ultrasonographic evaluation using the ACR TI-RADS, and had postoperative histopathological results. RESULTS: Seventy-one nodules from 67 patients were included. The median age was 51 years (range: 12-71). The overall malignancy rate was 20%. Among the nodules, 26 (37%) were classified as the nuclear atypia, and 45 (63%) as other atypia. The ACR TI-RADS score had a strong association with malignancy (p = 0.025). The presence and type of echogenic foci were associated with malignancy (p = 0.001). The malignancy rates for TR3, TR4, and TR5 nodules were 21%, 8%, and 55% respectively. CONCLUSION: The ACR TI-RADS was significantly associated with malignancy in both the overall AUS cohort and the nuclear atypia subgroup. The relatively high number of follicular thyroid carcinoma cases may have masked the predictive value of ultrasonography. The presence of peripheral calcifications was significantly associated with malignancy. Although the sample size was adequate by power analysis, larger cohorts would further strengthen these findings.

item.title: Platelet-rich plasma for post-tonsillectomy pain, haemorrhage, and wound healing: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

item.description:

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether intraoperative autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) reduces postoperative pain and haemorrhage and enhances wound healing after tonsillectomy, while critically evaluating the limitations that affect clinical translation and future applications. METHODS: Five databases were searched through 3 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing PRP with no PRP, placebo, or an untreated contralateral fossa. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty using GRADE. Random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were used for pain and healing outcomes; sparse haemorrhage outcomes were analysed using Mantel-Haenszel common-effect models with sensitivity analyses. Parallel-group and split-mouth trials were analysed separately. RESULTS: Twelve randomized trials including 723 patients were included, with 11 contributing quantitative data. PRP was associated with reduced pain on postoperative day (POD) 1 (MD -1.21, 95% CI -2.01 to -0.40) and POD 3 (MD -1.12, 95% CI -2.10 to -0.14), although effects were heterogeneous and transient. Primary haemorrhage showed a favourable common-effect estimate (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.07-0.80), but this was based on only 12 events and was not confirmed by random-effects sensitivity analysis. Complete healing did not significantly differ between groups (RR 1.34, 95% CI 0.59-3.06). CONCLUSION: PRP may provide a modest early analgesic effect after tonsillectomy, but current evidence does not demonstrate a consistent improvement in haemostasis or mucosal healing. Future research should focus on standardized PRP characterization, patient-level comparative trials, and direct evaluation of whether PRP improves tissue regeneration compared with other biomaterial-based approaches.

item.title: Modified barbed reposition pharyngoplasty with symmetrical flap for acquired nasopharyngeal stenosis.

Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867648



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Acquired nasopharyngeal stenosis (NPS) is a rare but serious complication following tonsillectomy or laser-assisted uvulopalatoplasty, leading to choking sensation and impaired nasal breathing. This study aimed to describe a modified pharyngoplasty technique and report its short-term outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on five patients with acquired NPS who underwent the procedure between 2017 and 2025. All cases were refractory to conservative treatment. The surgical technique involved symmetrical mucosal flaps combined with absorbable barbed sutures to achieve stable expansion of the pharyngeal airway. RESULTS: All patients showed rapid improvement in choking sensation and nasal breathing postoperatively. Normal speech and oral intake were possible from the day after surgery. During follow-up (5 months-2 years), no restenosis or major complications were observed, and endoscopic findings confirmed sustained airway patency. CONCLUSION: This technique can be performed safely in a single session without muscle resection or stenting and demonstrated favorable short-term outcomes. It may represent a practical surgical option for selected patients with acquired NPS. Further studies are required to confirm long-term efficacy.

item.title: Appropriate extent of endoscopic sinus surgery brings favorable therapeutic outcomes to chronic rhinosinusitis patients.
item.dc:creator: Tran T, Samuthpongtorn J, Seresirikachorn K, Chitsuthipakorn W, Hoang MP, Tran LV, Le MTQ, Anggraini D, Wardani RS, Mohamad S, et al.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: The optimal extent of endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) for patients with chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) remains undetermined. This study aimed to evaluate postoperative outcomes when the extent of ESS is concordant with the underlying pathophysiology. METHODS: This study enrolled 116 patients with CRS scheduled for three categories of ESS: limited ESS, full-house ESS, and extended ESS. Concordant ESS was defined as (1) limited ESS performed for patients requiring ventilation and drainage and (2) either full-house ESS or extended ESS performed for patients requiring access for topical therapies. Postoperative outcomes included symptom visual analogue scale (VAS), the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22), and endoscopic scores. RESULTS: At one year, patients receiving concordant ESS achieved superior outcomes in symptom VAS (mean difference [MD] 1.38; 95% CI 0.62-2.15; P < 0.01), SNOT-22 (MD 22.73; 95% CI 15.46-30.00; P < 0.01), and endoscopic scores (MD 6.48; 95% CI 1.96-11.00; P < 0.01). Limited ESS achieved better outcomes than extended ESS in SNOT-22 (MD - 21.05; 95% CI - 38.72 to - 3.37; P = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: The extent of ESS should be tailored to the underlying pathophysiology. Limited and full-house ESS are appropriate to improve ventilation. Full-house and extended ESS provide better outcomes when access for topical therapies is required.

item.title: Gasless endoscopic thyroidectomy via the transsubclavian approach: comparable safety and superior anterior cervical function preservation.
item.dc:creator: Huang C, Wang W, Yao J
item.description:
Authors: Huang C, Wang W, Yao J
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10641-x

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional open thyroidectomy (COT) for papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) frequently induces anterior cervical dysfunction and conspicuous scarring. The gasless endoscopic thyroidectomy via the transsubclavian approach (GETTSA) offers technical simplicity and superior cosmesis. This study assessed whether GETTSA provides adequate completeness of resection and effectiveness compared with COT while achieving superior preservation of anterior cervical function. METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive patients with unilateral PTC who underwent hemithyroidectomy between 2023 and 2025, with 37 in the GETTSA group and 65 in the COT group. Baseline and perioperative data were prospectively collected. Scar appearance and anterior cervical function were assessed using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS), Neck Impairment Score (NIS), Swallowing Impairment Score (SIS), and Voice Impairment Score (VIS) at 1, 3, and 6 months. Group comparisons were performed using t‑tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, or chi‑square tests, and generalized estimating equations (GEE) evaluated longitudinal group, time, and interaction effects. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics between the two groups were comparable. GETTSA had a longer operative time (P < 0.001) but less intraoperative blood loss (P = 0.002); hospital stay was slightly longer (P < 0.001). Parathyroid autotransplantation rates were higher in GETTSA (P < 0.001), yet postoperative PTH and calcium levels were similar. GEE demonstrated significant group and time effects for VSS, NIS, and SIS (all P < 0.001), with significant group‑by‑time interactions (P = 0.048, P = 0.026, and P < 0.001, respectively), indicating better and faster recovery in the GETTSA group. VIS showed a significant time effect (P < 0.001), but no group effect (P = 0.333) or interaction (P = 0.637). R0 resection was achieved in all patients, and no major procedure‑related complications occurred. CONCLUSION: GETTSA offers superior functional and cosmetic outcomes-notably improved swallowing function, better scar appearance, and reduced neck discomfort-with less intraoperative bleeding, comparable parathyroid safety, and adequate completeness of resection. Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore the relationship between recurrent otitis media (ROM), chronic media otitis with effusion (COM), and laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD) in pediatric populations. Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the potential benefit of survival of receiving timely postoperative radiation therapy (PORT) for head and neck cancer. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort. SETTING: National Cancer Database from 2004 to 2020. METHODS: Patients with a diagnosis of human papilloma virus (HPV)-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma who received adjuvant radiation were included. Exposure groups included timely PORT or delayed PORT (≤42 or >42 days from surgery to radiotherapy, respectively). The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival (OS). Observed OS was for the entire cohort, while predicted OS was for the generated model of universal timely PORT within 6 weeks. Survival analyses were replicated for demographic and clinical subgroups. RESULTS: In total, 58,184 patients were included. Patients were mostly male, white, and non-Hispanic. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This is a phase II subprotocol of the National Cancer Institute-Children's Oncology Group Pediatric Molecular Analysis for Therapy Choice (MATCH) precision oncology platform trial evaluating selpercatinib, a RET inhibitor, in children and young adults aged 1-21 years with relapsed or refractory solid tumors with RET alterations. RESULTS: Two patients with papillary thyroid carcinomas harboring CCD6C-RET fusions matched to the subprotocol. One patient was deemed ineligible as they had not yet experienced tumor recurrence. There were no dose-limiting toxicities, and the patient experienced only grade 1 adverse events (AEs) attributable to selpercatinib. CONCLUSION: There was a low match and accrual rate on this MATCH subprotocol, resulting in early termination of the study. The basis for low accrual was likely multifactorial, including the overall rarity of this genetic alteration across pediatric tumor types and accelerated FDA approval of selpercatinib in children ≥ 12 years old prior to the opening of this subprotocol. item.title: Mitochondrially Encoded Cytochrome C Oxidase 1, a Hypoxia- and Lactylation-Related Gene, Acts as a Tumor Suppressor and Therapeutic Target in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Zuo YD, Dong SD, Li JH, Li JC
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70475
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42867034



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aberrant expression of mitochondrially encoded Cytochrome c Oxidase Subunit 1 (MT-CO1) has increasingly been associated with tumor invasiveness and adverse clinical outcomes across multiple malignancies. However, its functional role and regulatory mechanisms in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remain poorly understood. METHODS: Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were integrated to identify genes consistently dysregulated across datasets. Candidate prognostic genes were subsequently prioritized using Cox proportional hazards regression in combination with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. A multi-omics validation framework was then applied, encompassing analysis of MT-CO1 expression in OSCC, protein-level validation using the Human Protein Atlas, and evaluation of associations with clinicopathological characteristics. The functional effects of MT-CO1 were evaluated in OSCC cell lines using gain-of-function assays. To assess the feasibility of pharmacologically targeting MT-CO1, molecular docking and subsequent molecular dynamics simulations were performed to characterize the interaction between amorolfine and MT-CO1; mechanistic rescue experiments were then conducted to determine whether the drug's effects were MT-CO1-dependent. RESULTS: MT-CO1 was associated with hypoxia and lactylation and was downregulated in OSCC, with lower expression correlating with poorer survival. MT-CO1 overexpression reduced cell viability, proliferation, and invasion while enhancing apoptotic signaling in vitro. Computational analyses further predicted a stable, high-affinity interaction between amorolfine and MT-CO1. Importantly, MT-CO1 suppression attenuated the antineoplastic effects of amorolfine in OSCC cells, supporting an MT-CO1-dependent mechanism of action. CONCLUSIONS: MT-CO1 as an underappreciated tumor-suppressive factor in OSCC and support further evaluation of amorolfine for therapeutic repurposing. MT-CO1 may serve as a biomarker of treatment response and that the MT-CO1-amorolfine axis may represent an actionable therapeutic vulnerability in OSCC.

item.title: Oral and Fecal Microbial Dysbiosis as Non-Invasive Diagnostic Biomarkers for Gastrointestinal Cancers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Hu S, Chen Z, Li Y, Liao Q, Luo M, Song D, Yu H, Gao Y, Yang S, Wan S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Hu S, Chen Z, Li Y, Liao Q, Luo M, Song D, Yu H, Gao Y, Yang S, Wan S, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70779
Published: 2026-Oct-13
PMID: 42865226



Abstract:
Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including esophageal (EC), gastric (GC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), impose a substantial global burden, with early detection remaining crucial for improving patient outcomes. The oral and gut microbiota are increasingly implicated in cancer development and hold promise as sources of non-invasive biomarkers. However, current evidence on microbiome-based diagnostics remains fragmented, and a systematic comparison of the diagnostic accuracy between oral and fecal sampling across multiple GI cancer types is lacking. To address this gap, a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus up to December 31, 2025, identified 43 case-control studies (59 cohorts) comprising 4452 cancer patients and 5809 controls. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) was 0.846 (95% CI: 0.824-0.867), though with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 86.5%). By cancer type, pooled AUCs were 0.746 for EC (5 cohorts), 0.886 for GC (8 cohorts), and 0.850 for CRC (46 cohorts). A bivariate analysis of 20 cohorts comparing sample types found no statistically significant difference in diagnostic performance between oral (sAUC = 0.863) and fecal sampling (sAUC = 0.820; p = 0.369). While these exploratory findings suggest that oral and fecal microbial biomarkers may offer comparable diagnostic accuracy for GI cancers, with oral sampling presenting a more practical option for screening, the results are preliminary. Significant heterogeneity, a limited number of oral cohorts, and the absence of clinical control groups highlight the need for large-scale prospective studies with direct comparisons and real-world validation to validate these biomarkers for clinical translation.

item.title: Familial Cancers Associated With Cancers of the Breast, Prostate, Colorectum, and Lung in Sweden.
item.dc:creator: Zitricky F, Sundquist K, Sundquist J, Hemminki A, Försti A, Hemminki K
item.description:
Authors: Zitricky F, Sundquist K, Sundquist J, Hemminki A, Försti A, Hemminki K
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70781
Published: 2026-Oct-13

Abstract:
Available epidemiological evidence shows that many cancers share familial risks, and this is increasingly confirmed by data on shared pathogenic germline gene variants between cancers. We decided to harness the world's largest resource on familial cancer to assess discordant familial risks for female breast (BC), prostate (PC), colorectal (CRC), and lung (LC) cancers with any of 22 different cancers in first-degree relatives (proband cancers). Familial relative risk was calculated as standardized incidence ratio (SIR) when either one proband or 2 or more (2+) probands were found in a family to distinguish low- and high-risk associations. Discordant familial associations of BC were significant for 12 1-proband and 5 2+ proband cancers. For PC, the numbers were 11 and 4; for CRC, they were 8 and 4; and for LC, they were 15 and 5. The results with large case numbers showed that BC, CRC, and LC associated with each other, but the familial association between PC and LC was negative. Many known or novel associations with possible genetic causes were found, including lobular BC with stomach cancer, PC with kidney cancer, CRC with squamous cell skin and thyroid cancers, and LC with gallbladder and endocrine tumors, the most common of which were parathyroid adenomas. Also, LC associations with esophageal and cervical cancers were unlikely to be due to smoking alone and require additional explanations. In conclusion, 2/3 of discordant associations could suggest low-risk genetic and environmental causation and 1/3 high-risk genetic causation, both waiting for experimental proof.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Among temporomandibular disorders (TMDs), the main arthrogenic entities are disc-condylar complex disorders and degenerative diseases. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of physiotherapy in patients with temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science until January 2026 to search for studies including patients with a diagnosis of intracapsular TMD as participants; physical therapy or physical therapy combined to other conservative approaches as intervention; placebo, sham treatments, oral pharmacological anti-inflammatory drugs, behavioral therapy, or other conservative approaches as comparison; maximal mouth opening (MMO) as outcome. RESULTS: Out of 1578 identified records, 10 studies were included. A total of 354 subjects were analyzed, of which 213 performed a rehabilitation technique and 141 were included in the control group. Although the randomized trials reported improvement in MMO, pain, and function, a major limitation was the lack of standardized physiotherapy protocols across trials. CONCLUSION: Findings from the present systematic review showed that physiotherapy (active and passive jaw exercises, associated with relaxation techniques) might improve MMO. Further studies with uniform protocols and high-quality randomized trials are needed to validate the efficacy of multimodal treatments in arthrogenic TMD subtypes.

item.title: Socioeconomic and clinical factors associated with odontogenic infection types among hospitalised patients in Periurban Ghana.
item.dc:creator: Okyere Boadu KA, Asante LS, Frimpong P, Johnson EK, Adu VW, Okyere Boadu R
item.description:
Authors: Okyere Boadu KA, Asante LS, Frimpong P, Johnson EK, Adu VW, Okyere Boadu R
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360737
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42862874



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Odontogenic infections may progress to life-threatening complications if not managed promptly, and socioeconomic circumstances have been linked to their presentation, particularly where access to dental care is limited. Because every patient studied was already hospitalised, this analysis addresses the clinical type of infection at presentation, not the risk of developing one. METHODOLOGY: A retrospective cross-sectional review of hospital records was undertaken at the Allied Ward of Sunyani Teaching Hospital (January 2021 to January 2025). Of 811 consecutive admissions, 525 were excluded: 509 for non-odontogenic conditions and 16 for records missing more than 30% of required clinical fields, leaving 286 complete records. Chi-square tests were reported with Cramer's V and Monte Carlo exact p-values where cells were sparse. Because the unpenalised model showed quasi-complete separation, the primary analysis was a Firth-penalised multinomial logistic regression, with abscess as the reference outcome. RESULTS: Adjusting for age, sex, employment, residence, recorded oral hygiene, systemic comorbidity and alcohol use, unemployment was associated with higher adjusted odds of Ludwig's angina (LA) and not abscess (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI 1.27-6.09), and rural residence with necrotizing fasciitis (NF; AOR = 3.62, 95% CI 1.33-9.80). Systemic comorbidity was associated with LA (AOR = 4.14, 95% CI 1.83-9.36), NF (AOR = 8.72, 95% CI 2.95-25.75) and cellulitis (AOR = 2.07, 95% CI 1.03-4.18). Absence of a recorded poor-hygiene entry was associated with cellulitis (AOR = 8.05, 95% CI 2.42-26.83), interpreted as a documentation artefact not a protective effect. Sex and alcohol use showed no association. Number of children, the sole source of separation, was not retained; its penalised intervals included 1. CONCLUSION: Unemployment and systemic comorbidity were associated with more severe presentations, and rural residence with NF specifically. Findings are associational and describe variation in infection type among admitted patients rather than infection risk, within a retrospective single-centre design.

item.title: Effects of Isthmus-Sparing Lobectomy on Thyroid Function: A Prospective, Multicenter, Comparative Study.

Published: 2026-Oct-12
PMID: 42861680



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prospective study evaluated the impact of isthmus management (isthmus-sparing vs. isthmus-removing lobectomy) on postoperative hypothyroidism risk. METHODS: Between January 2022 and March 2023, 326 euthyroid patients with benign or low-risk papillary thyroid cancer were randomized into the isthmus-sparing (IS, n = 164) or isthmus-removing (IR, n = 162) group. Administration of levothyroxine was limited to patients with overt hypothyroidism or symptomatic subclinical hypothyroidism. RESULTS: TSH levels were significantly lower in the IS group at 3, 6, 12, and 18 months ( p < 0.05 ). Euthyroidism maintenance was higher in the IS group (62.2% vs. 38.9%, p = 0.001 ). The IS group showed lower subclinical hypothyroidism (33.8% vs. 54.9%, p = 0.001 ) and hormone replacement rates (8.5% vs. 25.3%, p = 0.001 ). Overt hypothyroidism was lower in the IS group without statistical significance (6.1% vs. 12.3%, p = 0.057 ). CONCLUSION: Isthmus-sparing lobectomy better preserves thyroid function and reduces postoperative subclinical hypothyroidism and hormone replacement needs compared to isthmus-removing lobectomy.

item.title: Effects of Antimicrobial Mouthwashes on Oral Health and Blood Pressure: A Preliminary Parallel Randomized Controlled Trial.

item.description:
Authors: Bhowmick D, Nayek M, Aquil A, Rudra A, Mistry S, Nair V, Das I
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70537
Published: 2026-Oct-12

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although antimicrobial mouthwashes vary in efficacy and safety for managing biofilm-induced gingivitis, concerns remain regarding their potential to reduce nitric oxide bioavailability and increase hypertension risk. Therefore, we investigated whether octenidine is more effective and causes fewer adverse events than chlorhexidine, and whether antimicrobial mouthwash use increases hypertension risk. METHODS: In this parallel randomized controlled trial, 90 participants were randomly allocated (1:1:1) to rinse with 10 mL of 2% saline (Group I), 0.2% chlorhexidine (Group II), or 0.1% octenidine (Group III) for 21 days. Co-primary outcomes (clinical parameters and blood pressure) and secondary outcomes (salivary bacterial count, adverse events, and pulse pressure) were assessed over 42 days. RESULTS: At day 22, antimicrobial mouthwashes significantly reduced clinical (29%-52%) and microbial (> 92%) measures (p < 0.001), whereas saline produced minimal changes (p > 0.05). Salivary nitrate levels showed the opposite trend. Groups II and III showed comparable efficacy, but octenidine was associated with fewer adverse events. Although systolic blood pressure increased slightly in all groups, the changes were clinically insignificant. Elevated pulse pressure in antimicrobial groups returned to baseline by Day 42. CONCLUSIONS: Octenidine (0.1%) was safer and comparably effective to chlorhexidine. Short-term antimicrobial mouthwash had no clinically significant effect on blood pressure. item.title: Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction in Hypermobile Patients.
item.dc:creator: Menton SM, Fairweather D, Wilson FC, Zangerle DJ, Murphy EF, Darakjian AA, Thompson CC, Gajarawala SN, Knight DRT, Bruno KA, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Menton SM, Fairweather D, Wilson FC, Zangerle DJ, Murphy EF, Darakjian AA, Thompson CC, Gajarawala SN, Knight DRT, Bruno KA, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70980
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860825



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether patients with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) or hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and inducible laryngeal obstruction (ILO) have more voice, cough, swallowing, GI issues, and MC activation than patients without ILO. METHODS: This retrospective study of 2162 patients meeting 2017 diagnostic criteria for hEDS (n = 507) or HSD (n = 1655) who were seen at the EDS Clinic in Mayo Clinic Florida from November 2019 to June 2025 compared patients who screened positive for ILO to those who screened negative. Patients were examined for self-reported symptoms of voice, cough, swallow, and GI issues as well as MC activation. RESULTS: Among patients with hEDS or HSD, 23.1% and 17.1% respectively screened positive for ILO. Patients with ILO had significantly more voice, cough, and swallow issues than patients without ILO (all p ≤ 0.007). Both diagnoses had more gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) (hEDS: 55.6% vs. 40.9%, p = 0.004; HSD: 55.8% vs. 42.2%, p < 0.0001). Additionally, both hEDS and HSD patients with ILO self-reported 18 allergy-related symptoms more often than those without ILO and had higher MC scores indicating widespread MC activation (all p < 0.0001). Cough, dysphagia, and elevated MC score were statistically significant predictors of ILO in both hEDS and HSD within a logistic regression analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Chronic cough, dysphagia, and elevated MC symptom burden were the strongest independent predictors of ILO across both hEDS and HSD, underscoring the need for routine multidisciplinary laryngeal assessment in this population.

item.title: Trajectories of Plasma Epstein-Barr Virus DNA and Clinical Outcomes in Recurrent or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Treated With PD-L1 Inhibitors: A Post-Hoc Analysis of a Multicenter, Phase II Study.

Authors: Pan Z, Pei Y, Diao J, Gao K, Ge J, Qing Y, Wei Y, Peng X
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70473
Published: 2026-Oct-11

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable biomarkers for predicting clinical outcomes in patients with recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (R/M NPC) treated with immunotherapy remain limited. This study evaluated the association between longitudinal EBV DNA trajectories and clinical outcomes in patients with R/M NPC receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from a multicenter, single-arm, Phase II trial evaluating the programmed cell death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor KL-A167 in patients with previously treated R/M NPC. Plasma EBV DNA was measured at baseline and at each scheduled efficacy assessment, which was conducted every six weeks until disease progression. EBV DNA trajectories were distinguished through a logistic trajectory model. Multivariable Cox models were used to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for survival outcomes. RESULTS: We identified three distinct trajectories: persistently undetectable (n = 17, 13.8%), fluctuating (n = 40, 32.5%), and persistently detectable (n = 66, 53.7%). Compared with the persistently undetectable group, HRs of death were 4.96 (95% CI, 1.60-15.40) and 12.59 (95% CI, 4.01-39.51) for the fluctuating and persistently detectable groups, respectively. HRs of disease progression were 1.96 (95% CI, 0.97-3.96) and 3.22 (95% CI, 1.56-6.67), respectively. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that plasma EBV DNA trajectories could be a promising biomarker for monitoring treatment response and longitudinal risk stratification.

item.title: CyberKnife Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy for Reirradiation of Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Outcomes and Prognostic Factors.

item.description:
Authors: Sharon S, Qureshi MM, Keohan S, Luk S, Jang S, Truong MT
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70494
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860746



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is used for reirradiation in recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (RM-HNSCC), but prognostic factors remain unclear. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 36 RM-HNSCC patients treated with CyberKnife-SBRT (2009-2022). ENDPOINTS: local control (LC) and overall survival (OS), estimated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 8.5 months, median OS was 9.6 months, with 1- and 2-year OS rates of 43.5% and 34.2%. One- and 2-year LC rates were 55.1% and 34.5%, with median time-to-recurrence of 14.1 months. On multivariable analysis, smoking > 30 pack-years predicted worse LC (HR 5.68; 95% CI, 1.42-22.70; p = 0.014), while former/never smoking predicted improved OS (HR 0.26; 95% CI, 0.08-0.82; p = 0.022). Gross tumor volume > 37.0 cm3 predicted worse LC (log-rank p = 0.044) and OS (p = 0.003) on univariate analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Smoking history independently predicted LC and OS; larger tumor volume was associated with worse outcomes and may inform patient selection for SBRT reirradiation.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated experience with probe-based near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) system (PTeye) in parathyroid gland (PTG) identification during total thyroidectomy. item.title: Hypoxia-induced HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 signaling axis enhances proliferation of oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Wu K, Zhang S, Cao L, Wang J, Wang M, Zheng Z, Feng X
item.description:
Authors: Wu K, Zhang S, Cao L, Wang J, Wang M, Zheng Z, Feng X
Journal: British journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1038/s41416-026-03632-6
Published: 2026-Oct-11
PMID: 42860443



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hypoxic microenvironment, a common feature of solid tumors, is critically involved in driving cancer malignancy. This research focuses on elucidating the function of high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), induced by such hypoxia, in the context of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). METHODS: We first profiled HMGB1 expression patterns in clinical OSCC specimens and evaluated their potential associations with clinicopathological parameters. To functionally characterize HMGB1, we conducted in vitro experiments utilizing silencing strategies. The impact of chronic cyclic hypoxia and HMGB1 depletion on key cellular processes-including proliferation, pyroptosis, and cell cycle-was systematically examined in OSCC cells. Signaling activity along the HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 axis was determined by immunoblotting. Furthermore, in vivo relevance was substantiated through murine xenograft models and a 4-NQO-induced carcinogenesis protocol. RESULTS: Analysis of clinical samples revealed that HMGB1 is constitutively upregulated in OSCC tissues. This elevated expression demonstrated a positive relationship with both increased tumor dimensions and lymph node metastasis. Subsequent Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that heightened HMGB1 levels are a marker for unfavorable patient outcomes. Furthermore, in cell culture systems, hypoxia treatment significantly elevates HMGB1 expression levels in OSCC cells. Knockdown of HMGB1 expression inhibits hypoxia-induced NLRP3, cleaved-caspase-1, and HIF-1α expression. Hypoxia treatment markedly enhanced OSCC cell proliferation, induced pyroptosis, and alleviated G2/M phase arrest, while HMGB1 knockdown reversed the pro-tumor effects of hypoxia. In vivo experiments demonstrated that HMGB1 knockdown inhibited tumor growth, whereas NLRP3 or caspase-1 deficiency delayed oral cancer progression. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggested that HMGB1 contributes to the progression of OSCC and has prognostic value. Targeting the hypoxia-induced HMGB1/NLRP3/Caspase-1 signaling axis may offer a viable therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Regular post-treatment surveillance is associated with improved survival in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective study.
item.dc:creator: Wu CF, Pan QY, Yang YX, Kou J, Peng YF, Li-Lin, Ma J, Sun Y, Lv JW, Zhou GQ
item.description:
Authors: Wu CF, Pan QY, Yang YX, Kou J, Peng YF, Li-Lin, Ma J, Sun Y, Lv JW, Zhou GQ

Published: 2026-Oct-10

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Benefit of post-treatment surveillance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), characterized by high recurrence risk, remains unexplored. We explored whether regular post-treatment surveillance facilitates earlier recurrence detection and improves survival. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We identified 8,798 patients with non-metastatic stage I-IVA NPC at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. The 1-year landmark analysis was chosen as representative of surveillance patterns, dividing patients into regular and irregular surveillance group based on surveillance intensity. Cox proportional hazards models clarified the association between overall survival (OS) and surveillance intensity, with subgroup analyses stratified by clinical stage and pretreatment Epstein-Barr virus DNA level. Survival impact of surveillance imaging for local, regional, and distant sites were also investigated. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 64.8 months. 1-year landmark analysis comprised 4,078 and 4,720 patients receiving regular (≥ 4 visits in the first year) and irregular surveillance (< 4 visits), respectively. Regular surveillance was linked to shorter median recurrence time (26.1 versus 27.0 months) and improved OS (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.99; P = 0.032) after multivariable adjustment. Notably, patients receiving regular imaging surveillance for distant site had better OS (HR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.57-0.82; P < 0.001) whereas imaging for local (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.90-2.04; P = 0.140) and regional site (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.57-1.27; P = 0.428) did not. Regular surveillance patients with distant metastases exhibited fewer metastatic organs (P < 0.001) and earlier recurrence stages (P < 0.001), translating into prolonged post-recurrence survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58-0.80; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Regular post-treatment surveillance, particularly distant imaging, could improve NPC survival, highlighting an urgency for evidence-based post-treatment surveillance strategies.

item.title: Evaluating imputation methods for longitudinal clinical trajectories: Toxicities in head and neck cancer treatment.
item.dc:creator: van der Hoek L, de Vette SPM, Neh H, MacRae DC, Langendijk JA, Sijtsema NM, van Ooijen PMA, van der Schaaf A, van Dijk LV
item.description:
Authors: van der Hoek L, de Vette SPM, Neh H, MacRae DC, Langendijk JA, Sijtsema NM, van Ooijen PMA, van der Schaaf A, van Dijk LV
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111815
Published: 2026-Oct-10
PMID: 42858855



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Longitudinally collected medical data is often afflicted by missingness, making methods mitigating missingness valuable. This study evaluated nine imputation methods for longitudinal data, using toxicity scores measured at multiple timepoints resulting from head and neck cancer treatment with radiotherapy. METHODS AND MATERIALS: For four toxicities (xerostomia, dysphagia, taste alteration, and sticky saliva), toxicity scores at 16 timepoints (1 prior, 7 during, and 8 after treatment) were collected, resulting in 1442 patients with on average ∼11.6 available timepoints. Imputation methods ranged from simple to deep learning-based. Methods were evaluated using a systematic removal strategy enabling comparison of true and imputed values. Patient-level, cohort-level and downstream model evaluation was done, evaluating inclusion criteria for patients, training data requirement and modelling effect respectively. RESULTS: General imputation quality showed minimal differences between methods, except simple methods, which performed worse. For patient-level evaluation, it was found that when patients had <50% of timepoints available, imputation started to worsen. Cohort-level evaluation showed that advanced methods could reach good performances at low patient counts (150 patients) but were more severely affected by low average timepoint availability. Downstream model evaluation showed negligible differences between methods, other than simple methods which resulted in different model coefficients. CONCLUSIONS: It was found that it is best to avoid simple imputation methods. Furthermore, when applying imputation to longitudinal data practitioners should be conscientious about inclusion of certain patients and if their dataset permits the use of more advanced imputation methods.

item.title: Dose-effect analysis of late dental adverse effects following radiation therapy in survivors of paediatric head and neck rhabdomyosarcoma.

item.description:
